newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: U.N. envoy meets S.Africa's Mbeki over Angola.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy meets S.Africa's Mbeki over Angola.

text.p: The U.N. special representative to Angola, Alioune Blondin Beye, held talks with South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki on Thursday over the Luanda peace process, a spokesman said.

Mbeki, President Nelson Mandela's heir apparent, briefed Beye on their meeting with former Angolan rebel UNITA movement leader Jonas Savimbi earlier this month, his spokesman Ricky Naidoo told Reuters.
"He did meet the deputy president today. It was a briefing by the deputy president to the U.N special representative on the meeting which had been held with Savimbi," Naidoo said without elaborating.
Mbeki was also planning a trip to Angola next week as a follow-on to the meeting with Savimbi in South Africa's old Transkei capital, Umtata, his spokesman said. Naidoo had no further details.

David Wimhurst, spokesman for the U.N. Angola Verification Mission monitoring implemention of a 1994 peace accord that ended nearly two decades of civil war, said from Luanda that Beye was intending to meet Mandela on his South African trip.
"He (Beye) is involved in a series of very intense consultations with all the key players. This visit to South Africa follows on these consultations," Wimhurst told Reuters.

"President Mandela is probably one of the most widely respected figures in the world," he said. "He's a man of influence and that's why he's got involved, but he has made it very clear South Africa does not intend to take on a mediation role."

South African officials were unavailable to confirm a meeting between Mandela and Beye, and Mandela was locked in talks at a secret hideaway with his African National Congress on Thursday planning future government and party policy.
Angola's MPLA-led government and UNITA are trying to form a government of national reconciliation under the peace plan, but progress has been slow.
UNITA has proposed that Savimbi head the official opposition in parliament, rather than be a vice-president under Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos as the president had offered.
The new government is due to be inaugurated on January 25.
